title: Finite element analysis with AI
subtitle: AgentFEM introductory exercises
name: Name ____________________    Date ____________________
aim: Describe a finite element problem, check modelling conditions and assess results using theory and numerical comparisons. No programming is required; identify the geometry, material, boundary conditions and quantities of interest.
setupIntro: Use an AI assistant connected to a local AgentFEM installation. First send:
setupNext: Once available, send these instructions. Wait for the reply before sending an exercise.
steps: Read the problem and predict the direction and magnitude of the response. Send the prompt, then check the figure, values and units.
Complete the comparison, fill in your observations and explain the results in your own words.
Check the reference answers on pages 6–7. If results differ substantially, check conditions before refining the mesh or time step.
retain: Keep the model, a table of key values and a result figure for each exercise. Calculate in SI units and convert displayed values to mm, μm or °C as requested.
install: Setup: see the installation and AI connection guides in the references. Windows uses WSL2.
ack: Acknowledgments: We thank Professor Meng Wang of Beijing Institute of Technology for first proposing the use of AI-native finite-element simulation in the classroom, and Renzi Bai of Northwestern Polytechnical University for Windows installation validation and contributions to this handout.

lessons.title: Cantilever deflection
lessons.goal: Distinguish true displacement from display magnification and check load–displacement proportionality.
conditions: L = 200 mm; h = 20 mm; thickness b = 10 mm
E = 210 GPa; ν = 0.30; homogeneous isotropic linear elasticity
Left end fixed; total downward force 200 N uniformly distributed on the right end face
2D plane stress; small displacements; no gravity
tasks: Record the downward displacement at the right-end midpoint and check its direction.
Repeat at 400 N with all other conditions unchanged. Calculate the deflection ratio.
Compare with cantilever beam theory and discuss possible sources of discrepancy.
lessons.deliver: Submit the deformed shape, a load–deflection table and a short comparison with theory.

lessons.title: Thick cylinder under internal pressure
lessons.goal: Use an axisymmetric model and check radial displacement against Lamé’s solution.
conditions: Inner radius a = 25 mm; outer radius b = 50 mm; length 100 mm
E = 210 GPa; ν = 0.30; homogeneous isotropic linear elasticity
Internal pressure p = 10 MPa; zero external pressure; no end-cap load
Axisymmetry; zero axial strain; axial displacement u_z = 0 throughout
tasks: Check the directions of internal pressure and radial displacement.
Increase the outer radius to 60 mm. Keep inner radius and pressure fixed; compare inner-wall displacement.
Calculate analytical displacements for both radii and explain the effect of wall thickness.
lessons.deliver: Submit the radial displacement profile with the analytical comparison and a table for both wall thicknesses.
record: Outer radius 50 mm: ______ μm     60 mm: ______ μm

lessons.title: Steady heat conduction in a plate
lessons.goal: Distinguish prescribed-temperature and insulated boundaries, and temperature from heat flux.
conditions: Other boundaries insulated; no internal heat source; 2D steady conduction
tasks: Record the centre temperature and describe the profile along the length.
Double conductivity to 90 W/(m·K), without changing the boundaries. Compare temperatures and heat flux.
Derive the temperature profile from the 1D steady heat equation and use Fourier’s law to calculate heat flux.
lessons.deliver: Submit the temperature field, a table of centre temperature and heat flux for both conductivities, and an analytical check.

lessons.title: Transient heating of a plate
lessons.goal: Read a temperature history, compare transient and steady states, and test time-step sensitivity.
conditions: k = 45 W/(m·K); ρ = 7800 kg/m³; c = 500 J/(kg·K), all constant
Initially 20 °C throughout; for t > 0, left 100 °C and right 20 °C
Other boundaries insulated; no internal heat source
To 600 s; backward Euler; initial time step Δt = 2 s
tasks: Plot centre temperature and record values at 60, 120, 300 and 600 s.
Repeat with a 1 s time step and the same mesh. Compare temperatures at shared sample times.
Compare with Exercise 3 and justify whether the plate is sufficiently close to steady state at 600 s.
lessons.deliver: Submit both temperature histories, the four-time table, time-series files and your time-step assessment.
